insurer: ICICI Lombard General Insurance Company Limited
sumInsured: Not specified (varies by plan; room rent terms differ for up to ₹4L vs ₹5L+)

great.name: Room Rent
great.quote: For policies with Annual Sum Insured options Rs. 5 Lakhs and above, there will be no room rent capping.
great.reference: Benefits covered under the Policy > Basic cover > In-patient Treatment > i. Room Rent charges
great.explanation: For Sum Insured of ₹5 lakhs and above, there is no room rent capping. This reduces the risk of room-category based deductions in your hospital bill.

great.name: Restore Benefit
great.quote: We will reset up to 100% of the Annual Sum Insured, for any illness/disease/injury... For policies with annual sum insured Rs. 10 Lakhs and above reset benefit will be triggered unlimited times for any illness/disease/injury
great.reference: Benefits covered under the Policy > Basic cover > 8. Reset Benefit
great.explanation: Up to 100% of the Annual Sum Insured is restored after it gets exhausted, and for ₹10 lakhs and above it can trigger unlimited times in a policy year. This gives extra cover for multiple hospitalisations in the same year.

great.name: Built-in SI Buffer
great.quote: We will provide a Loyalty bonus of 20%... at the end of each Policy Year irrespective of a claim being initiated... Loyalty bonus can only be utilized when the Annual Sum Insured is completely exhausted... In the event of Claim... the credited Loyalty bonus will not be reduced.
great.reference: Benefits covered under the Policy > 17. Loyalty bonus
great.explanation: A 20% Loyalty Bonus is added each policy year even if you make a claim, and it can be used only after the Annual Sum Insured is fully exhausted. This works like an extra insurer-funded buffer once your base cover runs out.

great.name: Modern Treatments
great.quote: We will cover the Medical Expenses... for the below mentioned Technological Advancements and Treatments... up to the Annual Sum Insured.
great.reference: Benefits covered under the Policy > Basic cover > 3. Technological Advancements and Treatments
great.explanation: Listed technological advancements and modern treatments are covered up to the Annual Sum Insured. This helps you access newer procedures without a separate sub-limit being stated here.

good.name: Bariatric Surgery
good.quote: 7. Bariatric Surgery Cover We will cover medical expenses incurred in respect of Hospitalisation... for Surgical Procedure/treatment for Obesity... This benefit has a waiting period of 24 months from date of inception of the first policy with Us
good.reference: Benefits covered under the Policy > Basic cover > 7. Bariatric Surgery Cover
good.explanation: Hospitalisation expenses for bariatric (obesity) surgery are covered after a 24-month waiting period from the first policy inception. This is useful if you may need weight-loss surgery later, but it won’t help in the first 2 years.

good.name: PED Waiting Period
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of a pre-existing Disease (PED)... shall be excluded until the expiry of 0 Months/24 months (depending on plan opted) of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the first policy
good.reference: Exclusions > Standard Exclusions > 1. Pre-Existing Diseases - Code- Excl01
good.explanation: Pre-existing diseases are covered after 0 months or 24 months depending on the plan opted. If your variant has 24 months, you must complete 2 years of continuous cover before PED claims are payable.

good.name: Specific Illness Waiting Period
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of the listed Conditions... shall be excluded until the expiry of 0 months/24months (depending on plan opted)
good.reference: Exclusions > Standard Exclusions > 2. Specified Disease/Procedure Waiting Period- Code- Excl02
good.explanation: Specified diseases/procedures have a waiting period of 0 months or 24 months depending on the plan opted. If your variant has 24 months, claims for those listed conditions are not payable in the first 2 years.

good.name: Initial Waiting Period
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of any illness within 30 days from the first policy commencement date shall be excluded except claims arising due to an accident
good.reference: Exclusions > Standard Exclusions > 4. 30-day waiting period- Code- Excl03
good.explanation: Illnesses are not covered in the first 30 days from policy start, except accidents. This means early non-accident hospitalisations soon after buying the policy won’t be payable.

good.name: Pre-hospitalization Cover
good.quote: We will cover the Pre-hospitalization Medical Expenses... immediately 60 days before the Insured Person’s Admission to Hospital
good.reference: Benefits covered under the Policy > Basic cover > 4. Pre- Hospitalisation Medical Expenses
good.explanation: Pre-hospitalisation medical expenses are covered for up to 60 days before admission. This helps pay for tests and consultations leading up to hospitalisation.

good.name: Post-hospitalization Cover
good.quote: We will cover the Post-hospitalization Medical Expenses... immediately 180 days following the Insured Person’s discharge from Hospital
good.reference: Benefits covered under the Policy > Basic cover > 5. Post Hospitalization Medical Expenses
good.explanation: Post-hospitalisation medical expenses are covered for up to 180 days after discharge. This supports follow-up treatment and medicines for up to 6 months.

good.name: Air Ambulance
good.quote: We will cover the expenses incurred on Air Ambulance services up to the Annual Sum Insured...
good.reference: Benefits covered under the Policy > Basic cover > 10. Domestic Air Ambulance Cover
good.explanation: Domestic air ambulance expenses are covered up to the Annual Sum Insured. This can be valuable in emergencies where rapid transfer is medically necessary.

good.name: Domiciliary Hospitalization
good.quote: We will cover the Medical Expenses incurred in respect of the Domiciliary Hospitalization... continues for at least 3 consecutive days
good.reference: Benefits covered under the Policy > Basic cover > 12. Domiciliary Hospitalization
good.explanation: Domiciliary (home) hospitalisation is covered when treatment continues for at least 3 consecutive days. This helps when hospital admission isn’t possible but hospital-like care is needed at home.

bad.name: Proportionate Deduction
bad.quote: If the Insured Person is admitted in a room category/limit that is higher than the one that is specified... then the Insured Person shall bear a rateable proportion of the total Associated medical expenses
bad.reference: Benefits covered under the Policy > Basic cover > In-patient Treatment > We will consider a claim under this Cover, subject to the following:
bad.explanation: If you take a room higher than your eligible category/limit, the insurer will apply a rateable (proportionate) deduction on associated medical expenses. This can sharply reduce claim payout beyond just the room rent difference.

bad.name: Consumables
bad.quote: consumables (other than those specified in the list of excluded expenses (non-medical) in Annexure II.
bad.reference: Benefits covered under the Policy > Basic cover > In-patient Treatment > v.
bad.explanation: Consumables are not fully covered because items listed as excluded non-medical expenses in Annexure II are not payable. This can increase your hospital out-of-pocket for items like gloves, masks, and similar supplies.

bad.name: Restore Benefit
bad.quote: The Reset Benefit will not be available for an Illness /Injury or related complications including but not limited to any relapse within 45 days in respect of which a claim has been paid in that Policy Year for the same Insured Person
bad.reference: Benefits covered under the Policy > Basic cover > 8. Reset Benefit > viii
bad.explanation: Reset cannot be used for the same illness/injury (or related complications/relapse) within 45 days if a claim has already been paid in that policy year for the same insured person. This limits the usefulness of restore for repeat admissions close together.

bad.name: Specific Illness Waiting Period
bad.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of the below mentioned illness within 90 days from the first policy commencement date shall be excluded... i. Hypertension ii. Diabetes iii. Cardiac Conditions
bad.explanation: Hypertension, diabetes and cardiac conditions are not covered if treated within the first 90 days from policy start. This is a stricter early waiting period for common lifestyle conditions.

bad.name: Claim Intimation
bad.quote: The above information needs to be provided... within 10 days of Hospitalisation, failing which We will have the right to treat the Claim as inadmissible, as We may deem fit at Our sole discretion.
bad.reference: Claims Procedure > (B) For Reimbursement Settlement > i.
bad.explanation: Claim intimation is required within 10 days of hospitalisation for reimbursement claims, failing which the insurer may treat the claim as inadmissible at its discretion. Missing this timeline can risk rejection even if the treatment is otherwise covered.

bad.name: Co-pay
bad.quote: "Co-Payment" shall mean a cost sharing requirement under a health Insurance policy that provides that the policy holder/insured will bear a specified percentage of the admissible claims amount.
bad.reference: Definitions > Co-Payment; Optional Covers > 11. Voluntary Co-Payment
bad.explanation: An optional Voluntary Co-Payment is referenced, which means you may have to bear a specified percentage of each admissible claim if selected. Any co-pay increases your out-of-pocket on every claim compared to plans with zero co-pay.

unclear.name: Cashless Network
unclear.quote: "Network Provider" means hospitals or health care providers enlisted by an Insurer , TPA or jointly by an insurer and TPA to provide medical services to an Insured by a cashless facility.
unclear.explanation: Only the definition of a network provider is given, but the number of cashless hospitals is not stated here. You will need to check the insurer/TPA network list for your city before buying.
